newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican govt details new minimum wage from Dec 3.
newsitem.headline: Mexican govt details new minimum wage from Dec 3.

text.p: The Mexican Minimum Wage Commission on Sunday detailed the increases in the minumum wage to apply from December 3 in various parts of the country.
The increases, of 17-18 percent, had already been announced in the country's latest economic pact between government, labour and business leaders, signed October 26.

The commission said that in Mexico City, the states of Baja California and Baja California Sur, the cities of Acapulco, Ciudad Juarez, Nogales, Matamoros and Coatzacoalcos, among others in geographic area "A", the minimum wage would rise 17 percent to 26.45 pesos a day.

In Guadalajara, Monterrey, Tampico, Hermosillo, El Mante, Poza Rica and other cities in area "B", the minimum wage would rise 17 percent to 24.50 pesos a day. In area "C", comprising the rest of the country, the minimum wage would rise 18 percent to 22.50 pesos a day.

Minimum salaries for specific professions would rise by the same percentage, according to geographic area. The increases are higher than the stated inflation target for 1997, set in the economic pact, of 15 percent.
They also reduced the difference between area B and C minimum wages to 9.04 percent from 9.97 percent as part of a gradual move towards bringing the two into line.
